display.purpose: Hero title only. Set at tight leading (0.9) for large optical impact.

title.purpose: Programme event titles and musician names (h3/h4).

body.purpose: All prose content. 17px for legibility with an older readership.

label.purpose: Section kickers, role labels, event metadata. Always uppercase, always Jost.

motion.name: ease-state

motion.name: ease-menu

breakpoints.name: mobile

breakpoints.name: small

narrative.overview:
OrgelEvent's visual language is the view from the organ loft in the Grote of Sint-Janskerk at the last light of day: golden light raking across warm stone, the congregation below reduced to shapes, the air holding both ceremony and anticipation. The palette is not decorative — it is structural, borrowed from the materials of Dutch church interiors: aged parchment, pipe brass, vestry green, the deep chancel dark.

The system refuses modernity for its own sake. It is printed-programme precise: sharp corners everywhere, no radius, no shadows, no decoration that couldn't appear in a typeset pamphlet. Text is set for the reader who already cares — not coaxed, but trusted. The editorial voice is warm but never effusive. White space is deliberate; density appears only where content earns it.

Depth is achieved through tonal section shifts (parchment ground → nave cream → footer dark), horizontal rules, and typographic contrast — never through elevation, blur, or shadow.
keyCharacteristics: Zero border-radius throughout; sharp corners as a system-wide invariant
Two-font system: Cormorant Garamond (display, serif authority) + Jost (sans precision)
Flat, no-shadow elevation replaced by tonal layering between sections
Gold (pipe brass) as a rare accent: kickers, prices, dividers, decorative rules only
Deep green as the action colour: all primary CTAs and interactive elements
Single-page editorial long-scroll: hero → facts → intro → programme → musicians → exhibitors → practical → tickets → footer

rules.name: The Brass Rarity Rule
rules.body: Pipe Brass (#A87328) appears in at most two places per viewport scroll. It signals 'this matters' and loses that signal if overused.

rules.name: The No White Rule
rules.body: Pure #ffffff only as button text on dark backgrounds and inside the ticket form. Every background is Warm Parchment or deeper.

rules.name: The Uppercase Jost Rule
rules.body: Uppercase tracking applies to Jost labels only. Never set Cormorant Garamond in full uppercase.

rules.name: The Weight Floor Rule
rules.body: Jost 300 for contextual text only; navigation, labels, buttons use 400 or 500 minimum.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No box-shadows anywhere. Depth through tonal layering and border contrast only.

rules.name: The Zero-Radius Rule
rules.body: No border-radius anywhere. Every UI element is strictly rectangular.

dos: Do use font-feature-settings 'liga' 1, 'kern' 1 on all Cormorant Garamond headings.
Do set text-rendering to optimizeLegibility on all headings.
Do treat Pipe Brass as a punctuation accent: kickers, ornament bars, prices, and finale items only.
Do maintain Score Line (#DDD4B0) as the universal border/rule colour.
Do write buttons in title case, never uppercase.
Do keep all section-lead text at Jost 300 weight.
donts: Don't add border-radius anywhere — not to cards, images, ticket forms, or tags.
Don't introduce box-shadows; use tonal layering for depth.
Don't use pure white (#ffffff) as a section background.
Don't set Cormorant Garamond in uppercase.
Don't use Pipe Brass as a background or large fill area.
Don't use Jost below weight 300 or above 500 for paragraph text.
